newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak foreign minister resigns, reasons not given. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak foreign minister resigns, reasons not given. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]

text.p: Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik resigned on Monday, a senior foreign ministry official told Reuters.
"The minister has resigned, you will get an official statement giving the reasons shortly," the official said.

The minister's decision came after a weekend referendum widely boycotted by the population and declared void by the Central Referendum Committee, which had been seen in the West as a key test of democracy in Slovakia.

Hamzik, a career diplomat who became foreign minister last August, had been trying to improve Slovakia's image in the face of increasing criticism by Western leaders concerned with the state of democracy in Slovakia.

The last spate of criticism came in April from U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in April, who strongly criticised Slovakia's treatment of its Hungarian minority, the lack of opposition reperesentation in parliamentary bodies and government control over the public (corrects from "state") media.
